target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users invoking the Canvas `a2ui_push` tool with malformed or unsupported A2UI JSONL could dispatch the payload to a paired node instead of getting the same Canvas validation used by the node CLI path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canvas now shares one supported-dialect validator between the CLI `canvas a2ui push` path and the agent-facing `canvas` tool path. The fix stays inside the Canvas plugin owner boundary, keeps A2UI v0.8 payloads unchanged, and preserves the existing rejection for v0.9 `createSurface` JSONL.

## User Impact

Malformed A2UI JSONL and unsupported v0.9 payloads are rejected before `canvas.a2ui.pushJSONL` is invoked, so paired nodes only receive Canvas-supported A2UI payloads from either entry point.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: the Canvas tool now rejects malformed JSONL and v0.9 `createSurface` JSONL before node A2UI dispatch, while the Canvas CLI keeps the existing v0.8-only behavior through the same validator.
- Current-head proof at `5b13855b3269ebfddd363c5b709fa510d1a1e86e`: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/canvas/src/tool.test.ts extensions/canvas/src/cli.test.ts` passed with 2 test files, 26 tests passed, and 1 skipped.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode commit --commit HEAD` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: invalid `a2ui_push` payloads stop before `callGatewayTool("node.invoke", ...)`, and CLI A2UI push still reports the validated v0.8 message count for supported payloads.

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `01919448940`. Method: `directSessionReq` — same handler code path as WebSocket RPC (`sessionsHandlers["sessions.create"]`). All scenarios pass on both `gateway-server` and `gateway-methods` test configurations.

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed), Plugin B child has `pluginOwnerId` persisted, Plugin B can reuse its child, Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child, Plugin B fork child has `pluginOwnerId`
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated), child `pluginOwnerId` persistence (fork and non-fork)
- What you did NOT verify: Cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. These address ClawSweeper review findings that the fork-only guard left cross-owner parent hierarchy, inherited auth-profile selection, and other parent-derived session state available through non-fork `parentSessionKey` use.

---

target.title: fix(terminal): strip no-argument C1 CSI sequences in sanitization
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`stripAnsiForSanitization` (used by `sanitizeForLog` and `sanitizeTerminalText`) only matched C1 CSI sequences that had at least one parameter or intermediate byte (`\x9b[\x20-\x3f]+[\x40-\x7e]`). No-argument C1 CSI sequences such as `\x9b@` (ICH), `\x9bA` (CUU), `\x9bB` (CUD), etc. were not recognized, so the C1 introducer was stripped as a control character while the final byte leaked into log/agent-visible output.

This is the same class of terminal escape leak fixed by #103672, but for C1 CSI rather than C1 OSC.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced `PARAMETERIZED_C1_ANSI_CSI_PATTERN` (which required `+` parameter bytes) with the existing `C1_ANSI_CSI_PATTERN` (which uses `*`) in `SANITIZATION_ANSI_SEQUENCE_REGEX`. This makes the sanitizer recognize complete C1 CSI sequences with or without parameters, while still preserving truly ambiguous lone `\x9b` bytes (those not followed by a final byte) for the control-character pass to remove.

Updated adjacent tests so that lone-C1-control cases do not accidentally form complete CSI sequences.

## User Impact

Log messages, error strings, and sanitized terminal text now correctly remove no-argument C1 CSI escape sequences instead of leaving stray final bytes in model/LLM-readable output.

## Real behavior proof

Negative control (origin/main version of `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts`):

```text
\x9b@: stripAnsi=""  stripAnsiForSanitization="\x9b@"  sanitizeForLog="@"  <<< LEAK
\x9bA: stripAnsi=""  stripAnsiForSanitization="\x9bA"  sanitizeForLog="A"  <<< LEAK
\x9bB: stripAnsi=""  stripAnsiForSanitization="\x9bB"  sanitizeForLog="B"  <<< LEAK
...
input:    "clean\x9b@\x9bA\x9bBtext"
result:   "clean@ABtext"
expected: "cleantext"
```

Fix applied:

```text
\x9b@: stripAnsi=""  stripAnsiForSanitization=""  sanitizeForLog=""
input:    "clean\x9b@\x9bA\x9bBtext"
result:   "cleantext"
expected: "cleantext"
```

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/terminal-core` — 12 files, 77 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.test.ts packages/terminal-core/src/safe-text.test.ts` passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.test.ts packages/terminal-core/src/safe-text.test.ts` passed.

target.title: fix(update): warn about stale gateway when restart is skipped after version change
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale-gateway warning visibility for readers of issue #92241.

After a package-manager update (`npm install -g openclaw@latest` or `openclaw update --no-restart`), the running gateway process holds stale `require.cache` entries. Inbound messages can hit `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and be silently dropped while the gateway appears healthy.

`maybeRestartService` already printed restart-skipped messages, but they used `theme.muted` (dimmed/gray text) that was easy to miss in terminal output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Addresses ClawSweeper review feedback on the previous attempt (closed PR #94119) which placed a version-change warning inside `printResult`. That position fires before the restart flow, making the warning misleading when a managed service is automatically restarted.

This version moves the warning into the two restart-skipped paths inside `maybeRestService`:

1. **--no-restart path** — When the user explicitly skipped restart and the version changed, the message upgrades from muted gray to prominent yellow (`theme.warn`) and references issue #92241.
2. **No installed service path** — When no managed gateway service is found and the version changed, shows a yellow warning with the exact restart command.
3. **No version change** — Both paths preserve the original muted style for cases where only a patch/internal update ran, avoiding noise.

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw update --no-restart` with a version change now see a conspicuous yellow warning instead of a dimmed line they could scroll past:

Before (missable):
```
  Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
  Tip: Run `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates to a running gateway.
```

After (prominent when version changed):
```
  ⚠ Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed. Restart required
    to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
  ⚠ Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the updated
    modules to the running gateway.
```

Static behavior for same-version updates is unchanged.

## Evidence

Three forms of proof follow.

### 1. Real CLI output — version-changing `openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart`

The actual command was run on a machine with an active OpenClaw Gateway, upgrading to a newer version:

```text
$ openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart

Updating OpenClaw...

--no-restart is set while the managed gateway service is running; the package
update will not stop or restart that process.

Update Result: OK
  Root: /home/.../node_modules/openclaw
  Before: 2026.6.11
  After: 2026.7.1-beta.1

Steps:
  ✓ global update (23.07s)
  ✓ global install swap (1.02s)
  ✓ openclaw doctor (22.95s)

Total time: 48.85s

Updating plugins...
No plugin updates needed.

Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates
to a running gateway.
```

This demonstrates a real update with **version change** (2026.6.11 → 2026.7.1-beta.1) reaching the `--no-restart` path. The output shows the current-main muted "Tip" line, confirming the existing behavior that this PR upgrades.

### 2. Patched output — version-changed warning from the patched code paths

The exact conditional branches from the patched `maybeRestService` were exercised directly (no mocks, real `theme.warn`/`theme.muted` functions):

```text
================================================================
PATCHED OUTPUT — maybeRestService (direct function call)
================================================================

--- Path 1: no installed service, version changed ---
Gateway: not restarted after version change (no installed service
found). Restart to apply updated modules: `openclaw gateway restart`

--- Path 1b: no installed service, same version (no warning) ---
Gateway: restart skipped (no installed service found).

--- Path 2: --no-restart, version changed ---

Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed.
Restart required to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the
updated modules to the running gateway.

--- Path 2b: --no-restart, same version (no warning) ---

Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply
updates to a running gateway.
```

Paths 1b and 2b produce the original muted output (identical to the real CLI run in proof 1).  
Paths 1 and 2 show the new prominent warning when version changes — the exact code in the PR diff.

### 3. Focused regression test

Added a test case `"warns about stale gateway when --no-restart and version changed"` to the `updateCommand service refresh behavior` scenario suite. The test mocks `runGatewayUpdate` with `before: { version: "1.0.0" }` and `after: { version: "2.0.0" }`, then calls `updateCommand({ restart: false })` and asserts the log contains:

- `"--no-restart set, but the installed version changed"`
- `"stale module imports (issue #92241)"`
- `"openclaw gateway restart"`
- `"openclaw doctor"`

The test passes with the patched code and would fail on current-main muted output.

### Type check

```text
$ npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json
  (no errors — type-safe conditional formatting)
```

### Formatting

```text
$ npx oxfmt --check src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts
Checking formatting...

All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Whitespace

```text
$ git diff --check
```

target.title: [do not merge] refactor: flip sessions and transcripts to sqlite storage
target.body:
Related: #96625
Related: #88838

## What Problem This Solves

Completes the session/transcript storage flip tracked by openclaw/openclaw#88838 by making per-agent SQLite the canonical runtime store for session metadata and transcript events. Legacy `sessions.json` and active transcript JSONL files are now doctor import inputs or archive artifacts, not runtime fallback state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The accessor seams from the earlier work made a single storage flip practical. Shipping a mixed file/SQLite runtime would let session metadata and transcript rows drift, so this PR moves import, runtime access, retention, SDK cleanup, and ratchets together behind the permanent accessor boundary.

## User Impact

Existing legacy session stores can be migrated non-destructively through doctor dry-run/import/validate/inspect flows. Runtime session creation, resume, transcript append, compaction, and maintenance use SQLite rows; retention still exports archived JSONL artifacts before deleting rows so support and archive workflows keep inspectable artifacts.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(firecrawl,brave,web-search,web-fetch,models-config): use own-property checks for config field lookups
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

All runtime config lookup paths use `"<key>" in <configObj>` to check whether a config field is present. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so an inherited property (e.g. via `Object.create({provider: "malicious"})`) could be mistaken for an explicit user config entry and override the normal env/default path.

### Why This Change Was Made

Use `Object.hasOwn()` which only checks own properties — inherited prototype properties are ignored. Config objects are plain POJOs from JSON, so `Object.hasOwn()` behaves identically for all legitimate config shapes while closing the prototype-chain attack surface.

### User Impact

No user-visible change for normal config. Prototype-chain inherited properties are no longer treated as user config entries across all runtime config lookup paths.

### Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/firecrawl/src/config.own-entries.test.ts extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-tools.test.ts src/web-search/runtime.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-tools.fetch.test.ts src/agents/models-config.merge.test.ts src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts src/commands/doctor/shared/ extensions/brave/` — all pass
- `git diff --check` — no whitespace issues

实时运行时证明：继承的属性被忽略，自身属性被保留
以下终端输出来自独立 Node.js 脚本，在 Node v16.17.1 环境中运行，模拟了 PR 修改的 5 处 in → Object.hasOwn() 变更的实际行为。


LIVE RUNTIME PROOF: inherited vs own config property checks

```
Node v16.17.1
─── Scenario 1: Prototype-inherited 'firecrawl' on search config ───
search object created via Object.create({ firecrawl: ... })
  search.firecrawl (direct access): PROTO-key
  'firecrawl' in search (OLD): true
  Object.hasOwn(search, 'firecrawl') (NEW): false

  OLD code (in operator) resolves firecrawl config to: apiKey=PROTO-key
  NEW code (Object.hasOwn) resolves firecrawl config to: undefined ✓ (CORRECT)

  ❌ OLD BEHAVIOR: Inherited proto property leaked into config resolution
  ✅ NEW BEHAVIOR: Inherited proto property correctly ignored

─── Scenario 2: Own 'firecrawl' property on search config ───
search object with own firecrawl property:
  'firecrawl' in searchWithOwn (OLD): true
  Object.hasOwn(searchWithOwn, 'firecrawl') (NEW): true

  OLD code resolves: apiKey=OWN-key
  NEW code resolves: apiKey=OWN-key

  ✅ Both old and new correctly find own property

─── Scenario 3: Inherited 'provider' on tools.web.search ───
web.search object with inherited 'provider':
  'provider' in search (OLD): true
  Object.hasOwn(search, 'provider') (NEW): false
  OLD resolves provider to: "brave"
  NEW resolves provider to: ""

  🎯 EXACT FIX: Old code would see proto-brave as user's chosen provider
     New code ignores it → provider falls through to runtime default/env

─── Scenario 4: Inherited 'contextWindow' in model config merge ───
explicitModel created via Object.create({ contextWindow: 99000 })
  'contextWindow' in explicitModel (OLD): true
  Object.hasOwn(explicitModel, 'contextWindow') (NEW): false
  OLD: explicitPresent=true → picks value=99000
  NEW: explicitPresent=false → falls through to implicit=128000

  ✅ OLD would override with proto-inherited 99000 instead of correct 128000
  ✅ NEW correctly ignores proto value, uses implicit model's 128000

### SUMMARY

The fix changes 6 files, replacing `'key' in obj` with `Object.hasOwn(obj, 'key')`:
  1. extensions/firecrawl/src/config.ts       — firecrawl search/fetch config lookup
  2. extensions/brave/web-search-shared.ts     — brave legacy credential lookup
  3. src/web-search/runtime.ts                 — web search provider resolution
  4. src/web-fetch/runtime.ts                  — web fetch provider resolution
  5. src/agents/models-config.merge.ts         — model token/input override merge

Without this fix, any config object created via Object.create() with
prototype properties would leak inherited values into runtime decisions.
This is particularly relevant in config merging where the user wrote no
explicit value, but a prototype chain carries a stale or default value.

With Object.hasOwn(), only properties actually present on the object itself
(i.e., values the user explicitly configured) influence runtime behavior.

```
关键结论：

in 运算符会遍历原型链，把继承的属性误认为用户显式配置
Object.hasOwn() 只检查对象自身属性，原型链值不会泄漏到运行时决策中
自身属性不受影响（两种方式都能正确读取）
所有 5 处变更覆盖了 Firecrawl、Brave、Web Search、Web Fetch、Model Config Merge 中的配置读取路径

### Files Changed

| File | Changes |
|---|---|
| `extensions/firecrawl/src/config.ts` | `"firecrawl" in search/fetch` → `Object.hasOwn()` (2) |
| `extensions/brave/web-search-shared.ts` | `"apiKey" in search` → `Object.hasOwn()` (1) |
| `extensions/firecrawl/src/config.own-entries.test.ts` | New: tests for own-property behavior |
| `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | `"provider" in search/params.search` → `Object.hasOwn()` (4) |
| `src/web-fetch/runtime.ts` | `"provider" in params.fetch` → `Object.hasOwn()` (2) |
| `src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts` | `maxCharsCap/maxResponseBytes/provider/userAgent` → `Object.hasOwn()` (4) |
| `src/agents/models-config.merge.ts` | `contextWindow/contextTokens/maxTokens/input/reasoning` → `Object.hasOwn()` (5) |
| `src/cli/capability-cli.ts` | `"apiKey" in value` → `Object.hasOwn()` (1) |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.ts` | `"apiKey" in search` → `Object.hasOwn()` (1) |

## What Problem This Solves

`submitGeminiBatch()` reads the full error response body via `batchRes.text()`
on non-404 batch-create failures with no size limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

target.title: fix(models): preserve static provider catalog metadata
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Static provider catalog conversion did not preserve all provider/model metadata consistently. The concrete current-main gap is provider-level `params`: static-catalog rows can define provider request params, but the returned runtime model did not merge those provider params with model params.

This PR also makes the static provider catalog converter explicitly carry `compat` and `mediaInput` so the returned runtime model preserves the same schema-valid metadata downstream payload and capability code expects.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime should preserve schema-valid provider/model metadata when resolving static provider catalog models. This is a metadata-propagation fix in `modelFromProviderStaticCatalog`; it does not add a new config key, policy path, transport, or custom-provider tool API.

Reviewer scope:
- This PR proves static provider catalog params/metadata propagation into the resolved runtime model and OpenAI-compatible request params via production modules.
- This PR is intentionally scoped away from the separate live-session `Tool exec not found` issue.
- Current main already keeps normal configured-provider compat flowing in other paths, and tools are permissive unless `compat.supportsTools === false`; the changed path here is static provider catalog conversion.

## User Impact

Users and bundled/provider catalogs can define provider-level request params and model metadata without losing that metadata during static provider catalog model resolution. Downstream payload generation and capability checks then receive the resolved model shape consistently.

- Static provider catalog conversion preserves model `compat` metadata.

target.title: fix(googlechat): add timeout to Google auth fetch requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Google Chat auth requests made through `createGoogleAuthFetch()` — the shared fetch implementation injected into Gaxios as the Google auth transport — had no request deadline. Token refresh, cert fetch, and any other HTTP auth operation could wait indefinitely when a Google auth endpoint accepted the connection but never responded.

## Why This Change Was Made

A 30s request timeout (`GOOGLE_AUTH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`) is added to the single `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call inside `createGoogleAuthFetch()`. This brings Google Chat auth fetches in line with every other OAuth/token path in the codebase:

- Chutes OAuth token exchange (#102026): 30s
- MiniMax OAuth (#102862): 30s  
- Google Vertex ADC token refresh (#102050): 30s
- Google Chat cert fetch in `auth.ts` (#102924): 30s
- QQ Bot token (#102897): 30s
- Mattermost REST (#102027): 30s

The existing SSRF policy, dispatcher routing, body-size limit (1 MB), response buffering, and release lifecycle are unchanged.

## User Impact

A stalled Google auth HTTP request now aborts within 30 seconds through the existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` timeout infrastructure instead of leaving the Google Chat integration stuck indefinitely.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.test.ts` — 21 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.ts extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.test.ts` — clean.
- The focused regression test uses a real `node:http` loopback server that accepts the auth fetch without responding, and proves the request rejects with an `AbortError`/`TimeoutError` within the deadline.
- No open PR touches `google-auth.runtime.ts`; `auth.ts` (PR #102924) is a separate file covering a different call site.

## Summary

Fixes #53250.

When `host=node` exec approval is required but no approval UI is available, the exec approval unavailable path could still fall back to generic guidance:

`exec denied: approval required (approval UI not available)`

That tells the operator something is wrong, but not what to do next for a node-hosted command. This patch moves the recovery guidance into the shared exec approval unavailable renderer used by the current host=node exec path, then names two concrete recovery paths:
- open the Control UI with `openclaw dashboard --no-open`
- inspect pending approvals with `openclaw approvals get --node <id|name|ip>` or the resolved node id when available

target.title: feat(config): support externally managed GitOps config
target.body:
Closes #103606

Related: #55753, #59616, #83851, #89526

Prior related PRs: #90653, #96438

## What Problem This Solves

Kubernetes and GitOps operators currently have to choose between mounting an
externally owned config as mutable local state or replacing the pod when a
ConfigMap generation changes. That makes safe config changes drop active
sessions and lets OpenClaw write back into a source whose desired state belongs
to Flux, Argo CD, Nix, or another controller.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a host-only `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_MANAGED=1` ownership contract: OpenClaw
continues to read and reconcile the config, but all config-writing CLI and
Gateway surfaces reject before side effects. The Gateway watches both the
configured path and its bounded parent, reconciles Kubernetes AtomicWriter
symlink swaps in process, and keeps its diff baseline at the last successfully
applied generation so failed, ignored, and restart-pending generations cannot
poison later reload decisions.

The Kubernetes example now mounts a stable, read-only ConfigMap directory at
`/etc/openclaw-config`, keeps runtime state on the PVC, and avoids a config hash
rollout trigger. Nix keeps its existing ownership/error contract. General
`$include` dependency watching and a transactional redesign of OpenClaw's own
internal config-write pipeline are intentionally out of scope; settings already
classified as restart-required still use the normal lifecycle restart path.

## User Impact

GitOps-managed pods can apply hot-safe root config changes without restarting
the pod, preserving active sessions and in-memory state. Operators get a clear,
consistent `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_MANAGED` error from setup, config, agent, skill, and
plugin mutation surfaces instead of a late filesystem failure. Invalid external
generations leave the last applied runtime active until the controller publishes
a valid replacement.

## Evidence

- AWS Crabbox `cbx_cace403c44f7` (released), exact rebased head:
  - `run_d7143581a688`: 1,095 focused assertions passed across 9 Vitest shards,
    including real AtomicWriter `..data` swaps and an out-of-parent symlink target.
  - `run_853f68350f67`: `pnpm check:changed` passed core/core-test typechecks,
    sharded lint, script lint, dependency/boundary guards, and import-cycle checks.
  - `run_8437bd887cb6`: production `pnpm build` passed.
  - `run_39871951e7c7`: Docker config-reload E2E passed (build, live Gateway,

- `bash -n scripts/k8s/deploy.sh`, `kubectl kustomize scripts/k8s/manifests`,
  and `git diff --check` passed locally.
- Fresh autoreview completed clean after the final post-rebase integration fix.

target.title: feat: support GPT-5.6 Ultra across OpenClaw and Codex runtimes
target.body:
Related: #98296, #103324

Builds on #98333, #103510, and #103581. This integrates @anyech's original Ultra contribution and preserves J Cai's contributor credit.

## What Problem This Solves

GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna are first-class OpenAI models, but Ultra behavior was not coherent across OpenClaw's embedded runtime and the native Codex app-server runtime. Model, runtime, and thinking selections could drift across `/model`, live switching, fallback, and reconnect. The embedded runtime could also request maximum inference effort without representing Ultra's proactive sub-agent semantics.

Native Codex Sol/Terra use multi-agent V2, whose spawn lifecycle is emitted as `subAgentActivity` rather than the V1 `collabAgentToolCall`. OpenClaw previously ignored that V2 event: the child ran and replied, but no OpenClaw task row was created or delivered.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add canonical, explicit `ultra` while preserving legacy `ultrathink -> high`.
- Carry model, runtime, and thinking atomically through `/model`, `/think`, fallback, cron, ACP, Gateway, TUI, Control UI, channel commands, and plugin execution.
- Give embedded OpenClaw logical Ultra for Sol, Terra, and Luna: provider-compatible `max` wire effort plus run-scoped proactive sub-agents.
- Give native Codex Ultra for Sol and Terra, and catalog-supported Max for Luna.
- Rotate native Codex threads only when a model switch crosses the V2/V1 protocol boundary; Sol and Terra resume their existing thread.
- Mirror parent-scoped Codex V2 `subAgentActivity` into the shared task lifecycle while reusing the trusted child completion/transcript delivery path.
- Make effort fallback strictly non-escalating when live metadata has gaps.
- Extend live Docker proof for fresh OpenAI defaults, embedded OpenClaw Ultra, and native Codex model/runtime switching.

## User Impact

- Fresh API-key setup selects `openai/gpt-5.6`.
- Fresh Codex/OAuth setup selects exact `openai/gpt-5.6-sol`.
- Sol and Terra support native Codex Ultra; Luna supports native Codex Max.
- Sol, Terra, and Luna support logical Ultra through the embedded OpenClaw runtime.
- Native Codex V2 children now appear as real OpenClaw tasks and deliver their completion to the parent.
- Existing explicit choices remain sticky, turn-local fallback no longer overwrites them, and `ultrathink` keeps its established High behavior.

## Evidence

- Exact final head: `4484f8c18f88eeb7fbcfb094ea0fb6847ed8dec6`.
- Full changed-surface Testbox gate: production/test type checks, all lint shards, dependency and architecture guards, and runtime cycle detection passed with zero warnings or errors.
- Focused suites: 201 live-switch/model-fallback/hook tests; 855 stateless/runtime/Gateway/agent/OpenAI tests; 79 native Codex provider/thread tests; 151 runtime-thinking tests.
- Codex V2 bridge: 55 focused tests; SDK surface report: 9 tests and exact clean check at 10,490 public exports / 5,236 callable exports.
- Fresh autoreview: one duplicate-event finding fixed by accepting only Codex's authoritative completed activity phase; rerun clean with no actionable findings.
- Exact-head full release-gate CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29096850454
- Dedicated exact-head live GPT-5.6 runs:
  - Embedded OpenClaw Ultra across Sol, Terra, and Luna, with sanitized captured-request proof that every request used wire `effort=max`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29096851338
  - Fresh OpenAI API-key default (`openai/gpt-5.6`): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29096852039
  - Native Codex Sol Ultra, Terra Ultra, and Luna Max, including V2 task completion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29096852851

The release-gate build initially exposed an unrelated current-main Control UI raw-copy baseline drift from #103657. Main repaired that generated baseline in `53058123fc01`; this final head is rebased onto the repair, and the exact i18n check plus build-artifacts lane pass.

### Codex contract checked

Current Codex source advertises Sol, Terra, and Luna separately, carries `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, derives proactive multi-agent mode for Ultra, preserves model changes within a thread when the protocol version is compatible, maps Ultra to provider-compatible `max` only at the inference boundary, and emits V2 child identity through `subAgentActivity`.

### Known live-auth limitation

The available OAuth fixture is stale/reused and refreshes fail with `token_expired` / `refresh_token_reused`. API-key Docker runs are the authoritative live-provider proof for this PR; OAuth model-selection behavior remains covered by deterministic provider and setup tests.

target.title: fix(novita): discover live account model catalog for listing and runtime (#103532)
target.body:
## Summary

The Novita provider plugin only exposed its **static manifest catalog**, so `openclaw models list --provider novita` and runtime model resolution never saw account-available routes (e.g. the reported `novita/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`). This PR adds authenticated **live model discovery** — activated through the plugin manifest — with the static catalog kept as an offline/auth-failure fallback.

Fixes #103532.

## What Problem This Solves

After configuring a Novita API key, the model selector stayed empty and a configured model like `novita/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` failed at runtime with `Unknown model … no matching models.providers["novita"].models[]`. The shipped plugin returned only fixed manifest rows and never queried the account catalog.

## Root Cause

- `provider-catalog.ts` returned only the static `NOVITA_MODEL_CATALOG`.
- Provider-filtered listing returns manifest rows before consulting a live catalog, and the runtime unknown-model path rejects any model absent from the resolved catalog.
- **Critically**, the Novita manifest did not opt into live discovery, so `catalog.run` / `augmentModelCatalog` hooks stay inert in production (listing returns static rows before `catalog.run`; bundled loading skips `augmentModelCatalog` without `runtimeAugment`).

## Changes

- **`openclaw.plugin.json`**: declare `modelCatalog.runtimeAugment = true` and `discovery.novita = "refreshable"` so provider-filtered listing consults `catalog.run` and bundled loading runs `augmentModelCatalog` (mirrors `chutes` / `anthropic`).
- **`provider-catalog.ts`**: authenticated live discovery via the provider SDK cached live-catalog runtime (`getCachedLiveProviderModelRows`, SSRF-guarded, 5s timeout, 5min TTL). When discovery succeeds, **curated static metadata (reasoning, vision, context, pricing) is preserved for models the manifest already knows**, conservative synthesis is used only for new account-only routes. A custom Novita baseUrl suppresses discovery so the credential is never sent to the public endpoint.
- **`index.test.ts`**: regression coverage for manifest activation, live discovery reaching both listing and runtime-registration paths with a `Bearer` header, and known-vs-new metadata behavior.
- **`docs/providers/novita.md`**: clarify the bundled list is the offline fallback.

## Evidence

**CI:** all required checks green (types, lint, extension-package-boundary, extension-bundled, test shards).

**Credentialed live proof (real Novita API key, redacted `sk_***…*** (46 chars)`)** — driving the **real** `buildNovitaProvider` against the **real** `https://api.novita.ai/openai/v1/models` endpoint:

```
=== static fallback catalog ===
count: 6

=== LIVE account catalog (real Novita /models) ===
count: 139
discovery active (differs from static): true
includes reported model 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash': true
account-only routes not in static (sample): baidu/ernie-4.5-300b-a47b-paddle,
  baidu/ernie-4.5-vl-424b-a47b, deepseek/deepseek_v3, deepseek/deepseek-ocr, ...
known model kimi-k2.5 kept curated metadata:
  {"reasoning":true,"input":["text","image"],"contextWindow":262144}
```

This confirms provider-filtered listing surfaces account-only routes (incl. the reported `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`), and that curated metadata for known models survives the sparse live rows.

**Runtime turn:** a live chat completion returned `HTTP 403 {"reason":"NOT_ENOUGH_BALANCE"}` for every model (including known static routes) — the test account has no inference credit, so a completion cannot be demonstrated with this key. This is an account-balance limitation, not a code issue; the discovery/listing/registration path is fully exercised above.

target.title: fix: expose replayed chat.send errors to retrying clients
target.body:
Closes #103703

Related: #98203
Supersedes: #98206

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where backend clients retrying a failed `chat.send` with the same idempotency key could not tell that the Gateway had returned a stored result. A cached retryable error therefore looked fresh and could be resubmitted until the client's retry budget was exhausted.

## Why This Change Was Made

This replaces the broad metadata forwarding proposed in #98206 with a narrow negotiated contract:

- `response-replay` is an explicit client capability.
- The only wire metadata is the closed JSON shape `{ replayed: true }`.
- `RespondFn` keeps arbitrary diagnostic metadata in a separate log-only argument.
- Clients without the capability receive the unchanged strict response envelope.
- The official TypeScript Gateway client advertises the capability and exposes `GatewayClientRequestError.replayed`, providing an in-tree consumer.

`runId`, diagnostic `error`/`channel` values, and plugin metadata are never copied into the response metadata object.

## User Impact

Retrying clients can stop resubmitting the same idempotency key after the Gateway returns a stored retryable error. Existing clients and native apps that do not advertise `response-replay` see no new response-frame fields.

## Evidence

- Post-rebase focused run: 67 unit tests and 110 Gateway tests passed.
- Full TypeScript project graph passed: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -b tsconfig.projects.json`.
- Full build passed with the repository's no-pnpm fallback: `OPENCLAW_BUILD_ALL_NO_PNPM=1 node scripts/build-all.mjs`.
- Formatting passed for every changed TypeScript/Markdown file.
- Extensions and scripts lint shards passed; the changed Gateway responder passed targeted type-aware core lint.
- Protocol and Swift models were regenerated; `ResponseFrame.meta` remains optional with a default-`nil` Swift initializer parameter.
- Tests verify the strict schema rejects arbitrary/legacy metadata, legacy clients receive no `meta`, opted-in clients receive only `{ replayed: true }`, cached `chat.send` paths supply the dedicated wire argument, and the TypeScript client consumes it on request errors.

The live WebSocket capture in #98206 already established that the original responder path dropped metadata. This PR does not repeat that transport-only proof; it adds the consumer, negotiation, safety boundary, and client-consumption proof requested in the closing review.

target.title: fix(nostr): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Nostr outbound adapter (`extensions/nostr/src/gateway.ts:nostrOutboundAdapter`) had no `sanitizeText` hook. Core delivery (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts:889-896`) only runs the per-channel assistant-text sanitizer when the adapter provides one; without it, internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding is delivered verbatim into Nostr DMs. Users see raw banners like tool-failure markers and raw `<tool_call>`/`<function_response>` XML in their direct messages.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Root cause:** the outbound adapter omits the `sanitizeText` hook that strips internal runtime scaffolding before delivery, and the adapter's narrowed `Pick` type did not even include the field.
- **Fix:** add `sanitizeText` to the `NostrOutboundAdapter` `Pick` type and wire `sanitizeText: ({ text }) => sanitizeAssistantVisibleText(text)` into the adapter — the identical one-line hook already shipped to 13 sibling channels: twitch (#103109), mattermost (#98693), feishu (#98705), signal (#97360), slack (#97367), matrix (#97372), irc (#97214), telegram, googlechat (#90684), qqbot (#90132), discord, whatsapp (#71830), and sms.

## User Impact

Internal tool-trace banners and leaked XML scaffolding no longer reach Nostr DM recipients. Ordinary assistant prose is preserved unchanged.

## Linked context

N/A (no existing issue). Sibling fixes: #103109, #98693, #98705.

## Evidence

Terminal capture of `node --import tsx` runtime verification calling the **patched adapter hook** `nostrOutboundAdapter.sanitizeText` (exact hook added by this PR) on the exact PR head:

```
hook exists: true
[PASS] tool-trace banner: "Done."
[PASS] xml tool-call: "DM delivered."
[PASS] plain prose: "The relay has 2 active subscriptions."
```

The gateway inbound reply path now applies the same sanitizer before `reply()`:

```
[PASS] gateway deliver: strips banner keeps prose: "Done."
[PASS] gateway deliver: strips xml keeps prose: "DM delivered."
[PASS] gateway deliver: plain prose unchanged: "The relay has 2 active subscriptions."
```

Both the outbound adapter path and the gateway reply path strip internal scaffolding before delivery.

| # | Field | Value |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | Behavior or issue addressed | Nostr outbound adapter AND gateway reply path both delivered internal tool-trace scaffolding verbatim. |
| 2 | Real environment tested | Linux x64, Node 22; the patched adapter hook and gateway deliver callback invoked on the exact PR head (43283b42e4ad). |
| 3 | Exact steps or command run | `node --import tsx` script importing `nostrOutboundAdapter` (calls `sanitizeText`) and exercising the gateway `deliver` sanitize logic, plus colocated vitest. |
| 4 | Evidence after fix | Terminal output above: both the adapter hook and the gateway reply path strip banners/XML while preserving ordinary prose. |
| 5 | Observed result after fix | Tool-trace scaffolding is removed on both delivery paths; ordinary text unchanged. |
| 6 | What was not tested | Live Nostr relay delivery (no relay in this env); both code paths are exercised directly. |

## Tests and validation

New `outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts` mirrors the twitch #103109 test: asserts the hook strips banners, XML tool-call scaffolding, multiline function-response scaffolding, and preserves ordinary prose.

## Risk checklist

- [x] One concern, one PR — only the Nostr outbound sanitizeText hook (and the narrowed type that omitted it).
- [x] No config/env/default surface change.
- [x] No SDK/protocol/auth/provider behavior change (reuses an already-exported SDK helper).

target.title: Avoid full transcript parse during successor rotation
target.body:
## Draft Status

This draft is paused after a fresh correctness and performance review. The current head is not ready for maintainer review.

The sampled reader avoids materializing the full transcript, but its prefix safety scan still reads the old history linearly. On the current metric fixture it read `3,473,005` bytes for a `3,374,701`-byte transcript. On a same-shape 8.84 MB fixture, full rotation measured `45.603 ms` median and the sampled path measured `57.596 ms` (`26.3%` slower). The earlier `30%` speedup evidence is therefore no longer valid.

The review also found that message-only sibling branches and older compaction records can live entirely before the sampled tail. Preserving those semantics requires either scanning the prefix structure or having durable branch/carry-state metadata. Treating every prefix message as a fallback condition would remove the fast path.

## Problem

Issue #99190 tracks long-lived session transcripts whose JSONL files are read and parsed in full on hot paths. This draft explored one bounded slice: file-backed post-compaction successor rotation.

## Current Approach

- Read a small session-header window and recent tail.
- Align the tail to complete JSONL records.
- Use the sampled path only for the current transcript version.
- Scan older prefix rows for preservation-sensitive state and fall back to the full reader when the sample cannot prove equivalence.

## What Is Needed Before Resuming

- A durable index or checkpoint that proves branch and carry-state completeness without scanning the entire prefix, or an explicit decision to change inactive-branch preservation semantics.
- Exact-range reads that loop to completion or fall back on short reads.
- Sampled records normalized through the same canonical loader as the full reader.
- A strict differential evaluator covering message-only sibling branches, older compactions, legacy content normalization, malformed rows, short reads, and very large individual records.
- Fresh end-to-end timing and byte-read evidence after all correctness gates pass.

The existing focused suite on the draft head passed, but it does not establish the missing prefix completeness or a performance win.

Related to #99190

target.title: fix(agents): preserve ANSI sanitizer state across bash chunks
target.body:
Closes #103668

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running bash commands through agents could see ANSI/OSC control-sequence fragments leak into streamed tool output, final bash results, and full-output spill files when a process split a terminal sequence across output callbacks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix adds a reusable incremental ANSI sequence stripper in terminal-core and lets the bash output accumulator use one sanitizer instance for the lifetime of each command. This preserves streaming and bounded-memory behavior while keeping one-shot `stripAnsiSequences()` semantics unchanged for existing callers.

## User Impact

Bash output sanitization is now invariant to callback chunking for OSC and CSI sequences. Agents and users receive the same clean output whether the process emits a complete sequence in one callback or splits it across callbacks.

## Evidence

Before this patch, sanitizing `A\x1b]0;title` and `\x07B` independently leaked fragments such as `Aitle\x07B`; whole-input sanitization returned `AB`.

## Summary

Fixes #38570.

Include the requester agent's configured `identity.name` in the `sessions_send` agent-to-agent prompt contexts.

This updates the three A2A prompt builders used by the flow:

- initial `sessions_send` request context
- bounded ping-pong reply prompts
- final announce prompt

The requester name is resolved from the requester session key through the configured agent identity and injected as:

`Agent 1 (requester) name: <identity.name>.`

The rebased branch preserves the current prompt-cache contract from `main`: requester and target session keys still render as `<REQUESTER_SESSION>` and `<TARGET_SESSION>`, while low-cardinality channel names remain concrete.

Non-goals:

- no change to agent routing or access policy
- no change to target-agent identity handling
- no change to delivery behavior or ping-pong limits

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/sessions-send-helpers.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed:

- A2A prompt context should explicitly tell the receiving agent the requester's configured identity name instead of forcing it to infer from the session key

Local proof:

- exercised the production helper surface that renders the A2A prompt text
- added assertions for all three prompt shapes so the rendered context now includes `Agent 1 (requester) name: Stevo.`
- kept assertions that volatile concrete session keys do not appear in the system prompt context

Observed result:

- helper tests passed after plumbing `requesterName` through the `sessions_send` tool and A2A flow while preserving `<REQUESTER_SESSION>` and `<TARGET_SESSION>` placeholders

What was not tested:

- a full live multi-agent exchange in a running OpenClaw session

Why this is still meaningful:

- the user-visible behavior change is entirely in the prompt text built by the `sessions_send` helper flow
- the changed tests exercise the same prompt builders used by the tool at runtime

## Risk

Low risk.

This only adds one extra prompt line when the requester agent has a configured `identity.name`. It does not change session selection, visibility checks, channel routing, or tool authorization.

target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires
  - **records room event history exactly once across conflict retries** (new regression test for the narrowed boundary)
- Full local focused run:
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 120 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 22 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.abort-skip.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 198 passed
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary or a live Discord bot token, so a redacted live Discord conflict-to-success trace cannot be generated locally. Requesting maintainer help to run the Discord live transport / QA Lab proof on Crabbox, or a maintainer can trigger `@clawsweeper re-review` if the current in-process test evidence is sufficient.

target.title: fix(agents): lease session worktrees during runs
target.body:
## Summary

Session-backed managed worktrees are now leased and Git-locked for the lifetime of every agent run. Idle GC and a separate non-force remover both reject an admitted run's checkout, including when the run uses a subdirectory inside the worktree.

## Root cause

GC's owner-activity read and `git worktree remove --force` were independent operations. The previous patch repeated the read closer to removal, but a session could still be admitted after that read and while the destructive command started.

## Fix

The managed-worktree service now owns a per-worktree FIFO lease. `agent-command` acquires the lease before a session run touches its configured cwd and releases it in its outer cleanup. The lease retains the existing PID-tagged Git worktree lock, with local reference counting so only the final local holder unlocks it. All managed removal paths acquire the same queue through snapshotting and git removal; idle GC retains the owner-active guard after it has obtained that lease.

Lease lookup accepts a managed worktree root or one of its subdirectories, matching session worktrees whose configured workspace is nested below the repository root.

## Why this is the right boundary

The worktree service owns both the existing cross-process Git lock and destructive removal, so the same lifecycle primitive protects local and separate-service callers. Agent command is the session-run admission point that has the resolved cwd and can retain ownership through the actual runtime. Explicit removal keeps its existing force semantics, while an agent that loses the race before admission fails before using a deleted cwd rather than running against it.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`: 25 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/command/worktree-lease.test.ts`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`: passed.
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on `src/agents/agent-command.ts`, `src/agents/worktrees/service.ts`, and `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/worktree-gc-core.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/worktree-gc-core-test.tsbuildinfo`: clean.
- Structured local review: no accepted or actionable findings.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a resumed session must not have its managed checkout removed by GC or a separate non-force remover while its agent run is using that checkout or a nested workspace within it.
Real environment tested: pristine main `6eb9a5ada23b20353da9ef8e9fe69881567ca74f` and this patch `a3833de29a3c9ee0fe9405a929290bd6a737160a`, driving the production ManagedWorktreeService against real on-disk git worktrees and filesystem state.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: create a session-owned worktree, start a lease from a nested directory, attempt non-force removal through a second service instance, confirm that removal is rejected by the live Git lock, release the lease, then observe removal complete.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 6eb9a5a)
nested session directory exists while removal is pending: false
queued removal completes only after the active run ends: false
# AFTER (this patch a3833de)
nested session directory exists while removal is pending: true
separate non-force removal reports the live worktree lock: true
removal completes after the active run ends: true
```
Observed result after fix: a live session retains its nested working directory and blocks non-force removal until its lease ends, after which cleanup can complete normally.
What was not tested: no live provider request or multi-process gateway deployment was exercised; the production worktree lifecycle and real git filesystem operations were exercised in-process.

target.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws status [claw-or-agent]` for installed-agent, workspace-file, partial-state, and package-reference visibility
- add read-only `claws remove <claw-or-agent> --dry-run --json` planning
- require separate `--yes` consent before removing the Claw-created agent and owned state
- delete only unchanged managed workspace files and preserve local edits
- release skill/plugin provenance without uninstalling shared artifacts
- retain the install ledger when cleanup becomes unsafe after the agent config commit

## Scope

This is the status/remove slice for the grouped one-Claw/one-agent contract. Package names may resolve an install when unambiguous; final agent ids are always accepted and are required when the same package has created multiple agents.

Remove revalidates the agent config digest and managed files before mutation. Agent config drift and unsafe workspace paths block the plan. Missing files are treated as already removed, locally modified files are retained while their managed reference is released, and unchanged files are deleted through the existing rooted filesystem helper. Package references are released only after cleanup completes; the underlying skill/plugin remains installed.

If file cleanup becomes unsafe after the agent entry is removed, successful file-reference cleanup is retained but the root install and package references remain, so `status` and later doctor work can explain and retry the partial removal.

All commands remain process-gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`, and all new JSON contracts report `stability: "experimental"`.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- focused Oxlint on all seven changed files
- 18 focused status/remove and CLI tests
- 7 Claw lifecycle E2E tests, including real add/status/remove round trip

## What Problem This Solves

`downloadFile()` streams response body to disk via `pipeline()` without a byte
limit. A hostile server can send unbounded data, exhausting disk space.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `SKILL_DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (100 MiB) enforced via a Transform stream
counter inside the pipeline. The stream is aborted as soon as the byte limit
is exceeded — before excess bytes reach disk. The existing `finally` block
cleans up the temp file and releases the guarded response.

## User Impact

**Before:** no limit — disk exhaustion possible
**After:** 100 MiB enforced in-stream, excess bytes never reach disk, staging
tmp file is removed, and guarded response is released.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/install-download-maxbytes` | Base: `upstream/main` | Node: v22.19.0 — linux

### Real behavior proof

Two regression tests drive the real production `installDownloadSpec` entry point
(the exact function called by the skill installer). The HTTP layer is mocked
but the full production download pipeline — Transform counter, file write,
staging cleanup, and response release — executes exactly as it does in production.

**Test 1 — oversized download aborted mid-stream (> 100 MiB):**
- A streaming body emits 64 KiB chunks until the counter exceeds 100 MiB
- The Transform counter calls `file.destroy(err)` and `callback(err)`
- `pipeline()` stops forwarding chunks, the stream is destroyed
- Staging `.tmp` file is cleaned up by the `finally` block
- Guarded `release()` is called

target.title: fix(qqbot): guard mentionPatterns against ReDoS via compileSafeRegex
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a ReDoS vulnerability where operator-configured `mentionPatterns` in the QQBot
plugin were compiled with bare `new RegExp(pattern, "i")` without any safety check.
A pattern containing nested repetition such as `(a+)+$` compiles successfully but
causes catastrophic backtracking when matched against attacker-controlled message
content, pushing CPU to 100% and making the gateway unresponsive.

Attack chain: set `mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$"]` in config → attacker sends a message
with a long run of `'a'` characters → regex match never terminates → DoS.

The same class of bug was previously fixed in MCP glob patterns (#100330).
`compileSafeRegex` from `src/security/safe-regex.ts` is already exposed through
`openclaw/plugin-sdk/security-runtime` for exactly this use.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `new RegExp(pattern, "i")` with `compileSafeRegex(pattern, "i")`. The helper
rejects patterns with nested repetition and returns `null` for both unsafe and invalid
patterns, so the loop simply skips them — same observable behavior as before for valid
safe patterns, silent rejection for dangerous ones.

## User Impact

**Before:** An operator (or anyone with config write access) could configure a
`mentionPatterns` entry that causes the gateway process to spin at 100% CPU when
a matching message arrives.

**After:** Patterns with nested repetition are rejected at match time and skipped.
Safe patterns continue to work normally.

## Evidence

Node: v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64

**LOC** — `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/group/mention.ts`: +4/−5 (import + replace).
`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/group/mention.test.ts`: +20 (2 new regression cases).

**Before — catastrophic backtracking via raw `new RegExp`:**

```
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(20)+"b") →   65.5 ms
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(24)+"b") →  156.9 ms
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(26)+"b") →  640.7 ms
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(28)+"b") → 2522.4 ms  (2.5 s — gateway stalls)
```

Each +2 characters roughly 4× the time (exponential growth). At 64 characters the gateway
process would be unresponsive for minutes.

**After — `compileSafeRegex` guard, constant-time rejection:**

```
compileSafeRegex("(a+)+$", "i") → null (rejected before RegExp construction)
detectWasMentioned({ content: "a".repeat(24)+"b", mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$"] }) → false (0.065 ms)
detectWasMentioned({ content: "a".repeat(28)+"b", mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$"] }) → false (0.003 ms)
```

The guard rejects the pattern at compile time; `detectWasMentioned` returns `false` in
sub-millisecond time regardless of input length.

**Safe pattern still matches after a rejected unsafe one:**

```
detectWasMentioned({
  content: "hello @bot",
  mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$", "@bot"],
}) → true (0.130 ms)
```

**Regression tests — 24/24:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/group/mention.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ detectWasMentioned > rejects ReDoS patterns via compileSafeRegex guard    0ms
 ✓ detectWasMentioned > still matches safe patterns after a rejected unsafe one  0ms
 ✓ detectWasMentioned > ignores invalid regex patterns gracefully  0ms
 ... (21 more)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
   Duration  370ms
```

`rejects ReDoS patterns via compileSafeRegex guard`: passes `(a+)+$` with a 64-char
`'a'` input — asserts `false` is returned instantly rather than hanging.

`still matches safe patterns after a rejected unsafe one`: confirms the unsafe pattern
is skipped and the next safe pattern still matches.

What was not tested: live QQBot message delivery with a real QQ group.
Crabbox/Testbox remote CI was not run at submission time.

Related: #100330 (MCP glob ReDoS — same fix pattern)

target.body:
## Summary

Refresh Barnacle's candidate-label classification when a pull request moves from draft to ready for review.

## Issue / Motivation

Fixes #77343.

Barnacle currently misses the `ready_for_review` transition, so labels inferred while a PR is still a draft can remain stale after the author marks it ready. The previous candidate fix (#77361) was closed without merging, and current `main` still has the gap.

## Changes

- subscribe the auto-response workflow to `ready_for_review`
- treat that event as a candidate-label refresh event
- remove only stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels before adding the newly inferred set
- preserve labels controlled by explicit/manual flows such as `trigger-response`
- add focused regression coverage for draft-to-ready refresh and label preservation

## Testing

- `pnpm exec vitest run test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts` — 44 passed, 0 failed
- `node --check scripts/github/barnacle-auto-response.mjs` — passed
- YAML parse for `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` — passed (`yaml-parse=ok`)
- `git diff --check` — passed
- `gitleaks` scan of the change — clean
- manual secret-pattern scan — 0 hits

`actionlint` and `oxfmt` were not available in the existing checkout, so no dependency installation was attempted.

## What Problem This Solves

When a draft PR becomes ready, Barnacle now re-evaluates its candidate labels and removes stale Barnacle-owned classifications instead of leaving draft-era labels attached indefinitely. The cleanup is intentionally scoped so unrelated/manual labels are not disturbed.

## Evidence

- Focused Barnacle suite: 44 tests passed, including new `ready_for_review` refresh coverage.
- The workflow and script both include `ready_for_review`, closing the event-dispatch gap.
- Regression tests prove stale candidate labels are removed while manually controlled candidate labels remain intact.

target.title: fix(cron): persist startup catch-up deferrals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102236. A startup overflow catch-up slot could be persisted to SQLite while its protection marker existed only in memory. Restarting again before that slot fired let maintenance advance the job to its next natural cron slot, silently losing the deferred run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferral marker now lives on `CronJobState` as `pendingCatchupDeferral`, so the existing `state_json` persistence and rollback paths own the slot and marker together. The process-local Set and its parallel rollback bookkeeping are removed. Maintenance clears the persisted marker when the slot arrives, when no valid deferred slot remains, or when the job is disabled; execution also clears it after an outcome. Existing rows need no migration because an absent field means no pending deferral.

## User Impact

Overflow system-event cron jobs keep their staggered startup catch-up run across repeated gateway restarts instead of silently skipping to the next natural schedule. Unrelated stale future cron slots are still repaired normally.

## Evidence

- Real SQLite restart path: one service starts and persists an overflow deferral, a fresh service starts 3 seconds later against the same store, the original 5-second slot survives, executes once, and clears its marker.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.startup-overflow-clobber.test.ts src/cron/service.jobs.test.ts src/cron/service/ops.test.ts`: 3 files, 107 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service.restart-catchup.test.ts src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts`: 2 files, 81 tests passed.
- Oxlint passed for all nine changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.
