target.title: fix(agents): preserve runtime tool inheritance tokens for spawned subagents (#85030)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #85030: MCP/LSP/plugin tools not injected into subagent (sessions_spawn) sessions.

Deferred runtime selectors (`bundle-mcp`, `server__tool`, `lsp_*`, `group:plugins`) materialize into concrete tools only at runtime (MCP servers connect async, LSP/plugin tools build lazily). When a spawned subagent inherits the parent's effective tool surface via `replaceWithEffectiveToolAllowlist`, these selectors were absent from the synchronous concrete parent tool array and were silently dropped. The child then received only built-in tools, breaking multi-agent orchestration where worker agents need MCP/LSP/plugin tools.

### Root Cause

In all three spawn paths (`createOpenClawCodingTools`, `resolveGatewayScopedTools`, `resolveSkillDispatchTools`), the inherited allowlist was populated exclusively from concrete parent tools. Deferred selectors like `bundle-mcp` or `probe__search` have no concrete tool counterpart in the synchronous tool array, so they were dropped — even though the parent's policy explicitly authorized them.

### Fix

1. **Identify** deferred selectors with `isRuntimeMaterializationAllowlistEntry`
2. **Expand** each selector to its umbrella policy names (e.g. `probe__search` → `[probe__search, bundle-mcp, group:plugins]`)
3. **Re-filter** them through the SAME ordered authorization layers that produced the concrete parent tool set — security guarantee: a child can never gain a runtime the parent's policy denies
4. **Preserve** surviving tokens via a new `preserveRuntimeToolAllowlistEntries` option on `replaceWithEffectiveToolAllowlist`

Applied in three code paths: `createOpenClawCodingTools`, `resolveGatewayScopedTools`, and `resolveSkillDispatchTools`.

### Security Guarantee

Runtime tokens are filtered through every policy layer (profile, provider profile, global, agent, group, sender, sandbox, owner-only, subagent, inherited). A subagent policy that narrows the allowlist correctly strips broad tokens like `bundle-mcp` while preserving explicitly-allowed individual MCP/LSP selectors. The deny path works too: a parent that denies `bundle-mcp` prevents any MCP runtime from leaking to children.

## Evidence

### CI / Automated Tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-policy.test.ts src/gateway/tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts
```

All 121 tests passed (0 failures).

### New Tests Added (6 total)

| Test file | Tests | What they verify |
|-----------|:-----:|------------------|
| `tool-policy.test.ts` | 3 | Entry identification, policy-layer filtering, deny-layer removal of runtime selectors |
| `tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts` | 2 | Gateway path: token preservation AND narrow-policy filtering |
| `agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts` | 1 | Agent-tools path: token preservation in `createOpenClawCodingTools` |

### Real Behavior Proof

The fix was validated in the same scenario described in #85030:

1. Parent agent configured with `tools.allow` containing `bundle-mcp`, `probe__allowed` (MCP tool), and concrete tools
2. Subagent spawned via `sessions_spawn`
3. Child's `inheritedToolAllow` captured from session store
4. MCP runtime materialized for the child session
5. Child-visible MCP tools = intersection of inherited allowlist and materialized tools

Result: `probe__allowed` was present in the child's tool set; `probe__blocked` (not in the allowlist) was absent. The allowed MCP tool executed successfully via the production tool executor.

### Upstream Reference

Builds on the investigation and proof-of-concept from #92521 by @yu-xin-c.

target.title: fix(discord): keep thread-binding persona UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord thread-binding personas are built by `resolveThreadBindingPersona`, which clamps the `⚙️ <label>` display string to 80 characters with a raw `value.slice(0, 80)`. When an emoji or other astral code point straddles that limit, the raw slice keeps a dangling high surrogate, so the persona label used as the Discord thread webhook display name can carry a lone (invalid) surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the clamp through the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` primitive (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`), which backs off one code unit when the boundary would split a surrogate pair. The 80-character bound and the `⚙️ ` prefix are unchanged; the persona can only get one code unit shorter in the boundary case, never longer, and it is never emitted with a split surrogate.

## User Impact

Discord thread-binding persona names (webhook display names) stay valid Unicode. An emoji at the length boundary is dropped whole instead of surfacing as a broken/replacement character in Discord.

## Evidence

Real behavior at the 80-unit boundary (persona label = 50x U+1F600), using the exported `resolveThreadBindingPersona`:

- Before (raw slice): length 80, last unit `0xd83d`, `isWellFormed() = false` (dangling high surrogate)
- After (`truncateUtf16Safe`): length 79, last unit `0xde00`, `isWellFormed() = true` (complete pair)

- Added a regression test through the real `resolveThreadBindingPersona` path (an emoji straddling the 80-char limit), asserting no trailing high surrogate. RED before the fix (`expected true to be false`), GREEN after.
- `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.persona.test.ts` — 4 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `git diff --check` — clean

target.title: feat(exec): deny-over-allow exec approval denylist (#6615)
target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## Update — re-review 2 (clawsweeper P1 blockers resolved)

The previous review's three P1 blockers were "contract declared but not wired." All three are now wired end-to-end, with focused tests on each exact path plus refreshed real-behavior proof. Also merged latest `origin/main` (resolves the CONFLICTING/behind-main note).

- **[P1] Wire `tools.exec.denylist` into config schema + gateway caller** — `denylist` added to the strict zod `ToolExecBaseShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, non-empty-pattern refinement) so `openclaw config validate` accepts it and rejects malformed entries; threaded as `execConfigDenylist` through `agent-tools.ts` → `bash-tools.exec.ts` → `processGatewayAllowlist`, unioned across global + per-agent layers (`resolveEffectiveExecDenylist`). Tests: `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`.
- **[P1] Pass denylist hits into node-host `system.run`** — `invoke-system-run.ts` now evaluates the effective denylist (openclaw.json global + per-agent + `exec-approvals.json` file layer) and passes `denylisted`/`denylistReason` into `evaluateSystemRunPolicy`; the model auto-reviewer is hard-blocked on a hit (human-only), and unanalyzable commands fail closed. Tests: `invoke-system-run.test.ts` (+ node denial reason `denylist-hit`).
- **[P1] Add denylist to exec-approval protocol writes** — `ExecApprovalsDenylistEntrySchema` + `denylist` added to `ExecApprovalsPolicyFields` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts` so `exec.approvals.set` / `exec.approvals.node.set` round-trip the field. Tests: `exec-approvals-validators.test.ts`.

Two extra hardening changes made while wiring the above:

- **Real defect fix:** `sanitizeExecApprovalPolicy` (`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`) was silently dropping the defaults-layer `denylist` on every `saveExecApprovals` write — a routine policy write would disarm an operator's STOP list. Now normalized and preserved.
- **Standalone gate:** the gateway host now has an independent `requiresDenylistApproval || …` short-circuit in `processGatewayAllowlist`, so the deny-over-allow guarantee cannot regress even if `requiresExecApproval`'s denylist handling ever changes.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent), wired through both exec hosts (see Update above).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync (`*` → `[^/]*`, `**` → `.*`, `?` → `[^/]`).
- **Deny wins first**: a hit forces approval ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, on both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` (node denial reason `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Typecheck (repo's real TS-Go checker):** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both clean on this branch. (Stock `tsc` throws a bogus TS4058 in `src/secrets/config-io.ts` that tsgo does not — pre-existing on `main`.)

**Focused tests — all green on the exact paths flagged:**
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` — 19 (normalize/dedupe, both-layer union, exact/glob/basename/wrapper matches, conservative fallback, precedence).
- `src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts` — 19 and `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — 36 (node-host `system.run` enforcement, config-layer union, human-only, `denylist-hit`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 54 (gateway standalone denylist gate at `security=full`/`ask=off`).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts` — 8 (protocol/file denylist round-trip).
- `src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` — 39 and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 23 (config schema accept/validate + label/help coverage).

> Note: on a host that symlinks `head` to cargo-coreutils, one unrelated pre-existing test (`processGatewayAllowlist > uses a plan-backed enforced command…`) fails on a `/usr/bin/head` vs `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/head` path assertion. It is environmental and independent of this PR (our diff to that test file is additive only).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`, denylist supplied through the openclaw.json config layer exactly as the wired callers do):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Contract is now complete across config schema, gateway protocol write schema, gateway host caller, node-host `system.run`, docs/help (`schema.help.ts` + `schema.labels.ts`), tests, and real proof.
- No drive-by refactors.


## Node-host prompt parity (b0164f0fe8a, 2026-07-09)

Review found that the `host=node` `security=full`/`ask=off` fast path invoked `system.run` directly before prepare/approval registration, so a denylist STOP rule hard-denied server-side (`denylist-hit`) instead of raising the documented human allow-once prompt.

Fixed for prompt parity (recommended option):

- The direct fast path is taken only when the caller-visible effective denylist is **known empty**: the `openclaw.json` config layer is empty AND the node approvals-file denylist (fetched via `exec.approvals.node.get`) is known and empty. Fetch failures fail **closed** into the prepare path.
- On the prepare path, the effective denylist (config layer + node approvals-file layer) is evaluated caller-side; a hit forces a registered human approval request even at full/off, mirroring the gateway host: auto-review is excluded (human-only), and `allow-always` is downgraded to one-shot so no durable trust can be minted from a denylist hit.
- Non-matching commands with a configured denylist still auto-run (via the prepare path); setups with no denylist keep the direct fast path.

Focused tests added in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts`: config-layer hit registers an approval request (no direct denial), approvals-file hit registers an approval request, non-matching denylist auto-runs, known-empty denylist keeps the fast path, approvals fetch failure fails closed to prepare. `vitest run src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts --pool=forks` => 4 files, 146 tests passed; tsgo typecheck clean.

Honest proof status: production decision-function proof and the focused node-host approval-registration tests are in; a live gateway+node prompt -> allow-once -> runs-exactly-once capture is being prepared on a dedicated QA host and will be appended when complete.

Known residual (intentional, documented here): a denylist configured ONLY in the node machine's own local `openclaw.json` remains invisible to the gateway-side caller and still hard-denies server-side (fail-closed). The two operator surfaces this PR documents (`tools.exec.denylist` config layer and the exec-approvals file) now both get prompt parity on host=node.

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles
- `config:docs:gen`/`check` clean; generated config reference updated


### Current-head proof (SHA `368c1f48d14f8b1d0cf0378d227c9d8e639787af`)

Refreshed after the per-agent lookup fix. Redacted terminal transcript posted in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101248#issuecomment-4921711199):

- `routes parent-targeted completions to requester session without channel delivery` — `announceTarget:"parent"` wakes the parent session with `deliver:false`, no channel announce.
- `keeps direct external delivery for dormant completion requesters` / `does not raw-send channel completions` — default `channel` route unchanged.
- Routing + config suite: 348/348 pass at this SHA; `tsgo` core + core-test, import-cycles (0), and `oxlint` (0/0) all green.

target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` helper in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` was generalized to `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it can report the action (`delete` or `patch`) in its error message. `sessions.patch` now calls this helper both before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again inside `applyPatch` under the lock, matching the double-check pattern used by `sessions.delete`.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `sessions.patch limits plugin-runtime mutations to sessions owned by that plugin` in `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`. It verifies that a `memory-core` plugin-runtime client is rejected when archiving/unarchiving sessions owned by `other-plugin`, while patching a `memory-core`-owned session still succeeds.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch rejects plugin-runtime patches on legacy ownerless sessions` to enforce the fail-closed upgrade boundary.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch stamps pluginOwnerId when patch creates a new session` to prove owner propagation on creation.
- Added unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Focused local run:
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 260 passed across gateway-core/gateway-server/gateway-client/gateway-methods shards.
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → new ownership tests pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure caused by local `git` binary not supporting `git init -b main`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests run against a loopback Gateway server harness (`startGatewayServerHarness`), so the foreign-rejection and owner-success behavior is verified through real in-process plugin-runtime gateway wiring. This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary, so a redacted terminal log from a live deployed gateway cannot be generated locally.

target.title: fix(media): normalize uppercase FILE:// URI schemes in media directives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`MEDIA:` directives using an uppercase `FILE://` URI scheme are left in assistant text instead of being extracted as local media attachments. URI schemes are case-insensitive per RFC 3986.

Closes #103473

## Why This Change Was Made

Four locations in the media pipeline used case-sensitive `startsWith("file://")` checks:
- `normalizeMediaSource` in `src/media/parse.ts`
- The local-path heuristic in `splitMediaFromOutput` in `src/media/parse.ts`
- `resolveLocalMediaPath` in `src/media/local-media-path.ts`
- File-URL detection in `resolveLocalMediaFile` in `src/media/web-media.ts`

When a model outputs `MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/image.png` (uppercase scheme), none of these checks matched, so the directive remained as visible text.

## User Impact

Models that output `FILE://` (uppercase or mixed-case) URI schemes in media directives will now correctly have their attachments extracted, matching the behavior of lowercase `file://`. This fixes a case where a valid local media file would appear as raw text in the assistant response.

## Evidence

- Added test cases for `FILE://` and `File://` URI schemes in the media path acceptance table
- All 59 existing media parse tests pass
- Lint passes on all changed files

target.title: fix(agents): wake top-level requester when its last parallel child settles
target.body:
Closes #99395

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a top-level session (a normal chat/dashboard session, not itself a subagent) that spawns parallel subagents and waits with `sessions_yield` would silently stall after the last child finished: the parent never synthesized or delivered the final answer until a human sent another message ("are they done?"). Any fan-out-then-aggregate workflow is affected — e.g. the first-party `deep-research` skill ("Dispatches parallel investigators"). In the captured production incident (#99395), all 8 investigators finished within 2 minutes, the parent's last turn mis-named two long-finished children as "still waiting", and the session then sat parked for 5.5 minutes of total silence until a user ping rescued it. Results whose completion announce gave up (`NO_REPLY` retry exhaustion) were never heard at all.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime's "all descendants settled → continue and send your final answer" wake (`wakeSubagentRunAfterDescendants`, from the nested-orchestrator fix #97090) only targets orchestrators that have a subagent-registry run record; a top-level session has none, and the passive per-child announces give it no reliable way to know the batch drained (the injected `## Active Subagents` block vanishes at zero-active, and completion events carry no outstanding count). This change closes that gap at the runtime level: when a child reaches a terminal settle (announce delivered, given up, or suspended) and its requester has no more descendants awaiting settle, the requester receives a one-shot "all spawned subagents settled — synthesize and deliver now" wake through the existing announce delivery pipeline. Non-goals: nested orchestrators and cron sessions keep their existing wake mechanisms; single delivered completions and fire-and-forget children are deliberately excluded so one-at-a-time usage gains no extra turns.

## User Impact

Parallel fan-out workflows now deliver their consolidated final answer on their own — no more parked sessions that need a manual "are you done?" nudge, and results whose completion announce gave up still reach the user via the settle wake. Sequential single-subagent usage, fire-and-forget spawns, nested orchestrators, and cron jobs behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Focused unit tests** (new `src/agents/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.test.ts`, 13 cases covering drain gating, batch idempotency under concurrent last-sibling settles, wave scoping — including the staggered-wave transitivity case from review — and every skip guard):

```
✓ wakes the requester once with a batch-stable idempotency key when the fan-out drains
✓ computes the same idempotency key for concurrent last-sibling settles
✓ uses a new batch signature for a later second batch
✓ includes the whole connected drained wave for a staggered fan-out
✓ ignores long-settled children from earlier non-overlapping spawns
✓ does not wake while other children still await settle
✓ leaves nested orchestrators to the descendant-settle wake
✓ skips cron requester sessions
✓ skips requesters whose session entry is gone
✓ does not add a wake turn after a single delivered completion
✓ wakes for a single required completion whose announce never delivered
✓ stays out of pure fire-and-forget batches
✓ returns false when delivery fails without throwing

Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  13 passed (13)
```

**Full subagent unit + e2e sweep** (all 33 `src/agents/subagent-*` / `openclaw-tools.subagents.*` unit files, plus the 4 subagent e2e files including the nested-orchestrator and lifecycle-retry-grace suites):

```
Test Files  33 passed (33)   Tests  518 passed (518)   [unit, 2 shards]
Test Files   4 passed (4)    Tests  104 passed (104)   [e2e]
```

`pnpm tsgo` (core + test tsconfigs), oxlint, oxfmt, and a full `pnpm build` also pass.

**Give-up path proven in-repo:** `subagent-registry.lifecycle-retry-grace.e2e.test.ts` ("cancels timeout grace…") drives a real completion announce to retry exhaustion → suspension, and asserts exactly one `announce:requester-settle:…` wake follows it and that no timeout completion re-announces — the `NO_REPLY` give-up class from the incident, reproduced against the real registry/lifecycle modules.

**After-fix real-run proof #2 — the production failure class, rescued (2026-07-03, redacted):** a real gateway built from this branch, isolated state dir, real model (`claude-sonnet-4-6` via an OpenAI-compatible proxy), driven by exactly one user message: a deep-research skill task that fanned out **8 investigators in two batches** (5-concurrency staggering, one spawn attempt failed and was retried by the parent), each writing a multi-section report over ~5 minutes. This reproduces the linked incident's shape — and its failure mode fired en masse:

```
14:34:41  user sends the research task                        [the ONLY user message]
14:35:0x  parent spawns 8 investigators (2 batches), yields
14:40–14:53  11 child runs end (incl. parent-driven re-dispatches); EIGHT completion
          announces exhaust retries and give up ("completion agent did not produce a
          visible reply") — the parent NO_REPLYs essentially every completion event.
          On unpatched openclaw this session is now permanently parked.
14:53:01  last child settles → drain
14:53:02  settle wake attempt 1 dispatched; its turn begins "All 8 investigators have
          now reported… Writing the final report" → provider stream stalls mid-
          synthesis → run dies (LLM request timed out) at 14:55:21
14:55:31  hardening retry (`…:retry-1` key, 30 s backoff) → wake turn runs 4.7 min →
15:00:16  completes, delivering the FULL ~48,000-char final report into the session
14:59:31  precautionary attempt 3 (`…:retry-2`, dispatched while attempt 2's RPC await
          timed out) → queued turn replies NO_REPLY (report already delivered) — the
          escape hatch bounds duplicates
```

Consolidated report delivered with **0 post-yield user messages**, through eight announce give-ups AND a dead first wake turn. The retry hardening (second commit) exists because an earlier identical run showed the one-shot wake turn dying to the same provider stall and re-parking the session — the retry + fresh-suffix idempotency design was validated live within the same evening.

**After-fix real-run proof #1 — clean mechanics (2026-07-03, redacted):** same setup, one user message: *"Spawn exactly THREE subagents in parallel via sessions_spawn … sessions_yield … send one consolidated summary titled ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP."* No further input was sent. Timeline (UTC, from the gateway log + the `agent:main:main` session transcript):

```
11:03:47  user turn (the ONLY user message)
11:04:04  parent spawns 3 children, yields: "All three subagents spawned. Waiting for all to complete."
11:04:18  child run cde92f71 ended (stopReason=stop)          [gateway log]
11:04:18  child run 5e0e8996 ended (stopReason=stop)
11:04:19  parent replies NO_REPLY to the first completion event
11:04:22  parent, on the second completion event: "Still waiting for the honeybee-facts
          subagent before sending the consolidated summary."   [accurate at that moment —
                                                                honeybee was still running]
11:04:25  child run f4c9f1fa (honeybee) ended (stopReason=stop) [last child settles]
11:04:26  final completion announce reaches the parent
11:04:27  parent: "All three are in. Here's the consolidated summary: # ANIMAL FACTS ROUNDUP …"
11:04:45  run announce:requester-settle:agent:main:main:5e0e8996…,cde92f71…,f4c9f1fa… ended
          [the new settle wake — batch-stable idempotency key covering all 3 children, carrying
           "[Subagent Context] Every subagent spawned from this session has now settled … send your
           consolidated final answer to the user now" + all three children's findings]
11:04:45  parent replies NO_REPLY to the wake                   [answer already delivered — the
                                                                escape hatch suppressing a duplicate]
```

Consolidated final answer delivered ~2 s after the last child settled, with **0 post-yield user messages**. In this run the parent synthesized correctly on the final announce turn itself; the settle wake then fired at drain exactly as designed — one turn, batch-stable `requester-settle` key covering all three children, full findings attached — and its `NO_REPLY` escape hatch correctly absorbed it without a duplicate message. That is the designed division of labor: when the parent handles the last announce well (as here), the wake is a silent no-op; when it doesn't (the production incident replied `NO_REPLY`/mis-tracked on the final announce and parked for 5.5 minutes), the wake is the turn that forces the synthesis, carrying everything needed to produce it.

**Live observation (production, openclaw 2026.6.10):** the incident in #99395 — gateway logs show all 8 children ended by 09:15:17 UTC, the parent's final turn at 09:15:25 mis-tracked two finished children as pending, then zero subagent/announce/resume activity for 5.5 minutes until the user's 09:20:45 ping. With this change the wake fires seconds after the last settle (see the incident walk-through in the issue for the full endedAt/announce table); the same fleet's prompt-policy mitigation had already been shown insufficient (it was fully deployed and still parked).

**Idempotency under race:** concurrent last-sibling settles compute the same `requester-settle:<requesterKey>:<sorted runIds>` key (unit-tested), so the gateway collapses double-fires into one wake turn; the wake message additionally instructs `NO_REPLY` if the consolidated answer was already delivered, so the worst case of any dedupe miss is one silent turn.

**CI note:** the QA Smoke CI failure on this PR is a single scenario, `personal-tool-safety-followthrough` (80/81 scenarios passed) — a personal tool-safety flow that spawns no subagents and never reaches the changed code (`qa/scenarios/personal/tool-safety-followthrough.yaml` contains no `sessions_spawn`/`sessions_yield`/subagent usage; the settle-wake trigger only fires from subagent-run finalize paths). The same job is currently red on `main` itself with a different scenario each run (`native-command-session-target` in [run 28642974038](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28642974038) and [run 28641562098](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28641562098)), consistent with a one-of-N scenario flake rather than a regression from this change. Happy to have the job re-run.

## Implementation notes

- **`hasDescendantRunAwaitingSettle`** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-queries.ts`): early-exit drain check where a *suspended* final delivery counts as settled — suspension is terminal for automatic announce retries, so a requester-drain decision must not wait on it (with `countPendingDescendantRuns` semantics the drain would never reach zero in exactly the incident scenario: 2 of 8 announces gave up and suspended). Implemented as an option on the shared `countPendingDescendantRunsInternal` visitor, so the pending and settle definitions cannot drift.
- **`maybeWakeRequesterAfterAllChildrenSettled`** (`src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`): scopes the wake batch to the settling child's **parallel wave — the connected component of lifetime overlaps** seeded at the settling run. Membership is transitive, not direct-overlap-only (per review): in a staggered fan-out where A overlaps B and B overlaps C but A never overlaps C, the wake at C's settle still carries A's results, and every possible last-settler computes the same component so the idempotency key stays batch-stable. Long-settled children from earlier spawns whose lifetimes never chain into the wave stay out, so a later one-off completion never re-wakes the requester about old results. Fires only for ≥ 2 required completions in the wave or ≥ 1 undelivered required completion; skips nested (depth ≥ 1) and cron requesters; defers session-store reads until the in-memory registry gating passes (this runs on every child settle fleet-wide); reuses `buildChildCompletionFindings` so the wake carries the wave's results; delivers via `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` (active requesters get it steered into the live turn, parked ones get a new origin-routed turn).
- **Trigger seams** (`src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts`): fires from `completeCleanupBookkeeping` (the funnel all cleanup-terminal paths share) and from `suspendPendingFinalDelivery`; the suspended-delivery discard sweep passes `skipRequesterSettleWake` so a 24 h-later discard cannot re-wake. Fire-and-forget — settle bookkeeping never blocks on the wake.
- **Transient-failure retry** (second commit): the settle wake is the only event that ever fires after a drain, so a wake turn lost to a provider stall would re-park the requester permanently (observed live — see Evidence). Bounded recovery: up to 3 attempts with 30 s/120 s backoff, each retry under a fresh `:retry-N` idempotency suffix (the gateway dedupe caches terminal run outcomes per key, so re-dispatching the same key would no-op). A legitimately silent wake reply already classifies as delivered and never retries; terminal failures and an abandoned requester stop immediately.
- **Why source, not a prompt/dist mitigation:** parking is *defined by* no turn running, so prompt-assembly mitigations can only decorate turns that occur — they cannot create the wake turn. A downstream fleet's compiled-dist attempts hit exactly the races resolved here at the source seams (last-sibling detection, give-up/suspension semantics, idempotency).
- **Scope note:** delete-cleanup children leave the registry at settle, so a pure delete-mode fan-out gets partial/no findings in the wake message (the parking class observed in production is keep-mode).
- Release note: fixed top-level sessions parking after parallel subagent fan-outs — the requester is now woken to synthesize when its last child settles, including when a child's completion announce gave up.

target.title: fix(plugins): accept null optional metadata in approval requests
target.body:
Closes #98403

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `plugin.approval.request` rejected requests whose optional metadata fields were serialized as `null`. Callers that normalize missing optional metadata to `null` (for example, bridge callers serializing absent plugin IDs, tool IDs, severity, or turn-source routing fields) received `INVALID_REQUEST` before the approval could be registered or routed — even though the gateway handler already treats every one of these fields as `string | null` and normalizes them via `normalizeOptionalString`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The validation schema was the sole holdout: `PluginApprovalRequestParamsSchema` declared each optional metadata field as `Type.Optional(Type.String())` (or `NonEmptyString` / the decision array) with no `Type.Null()` alternative, under `additionalProperties: false`, so a literal `null` failed validation before the handler's nullable-normalization path could run.

This adds `Type.Null()` to the optional metadata fields (`pluginId`, `severity`, `toolName`, `toolCallId`, `allowedDecisions`, `agentId`, `sessionKey`, `turnSourceChannel/To/AccountId/ThreadId`), mirroring the nullable pattern the sibling `ExecApproval` request schema already uses for the same routing fields. The change is strictly a relaxation: omitted still works, a present string still works, and now `null` is also accepted. `additionalProperties: false` and the required `title` / `description` / `timeoutMs` / `twoPhase` contract are unchanged; `approvalReviewerDeviceIds` is left untouched because the handler does not treat it as nullable.

A focused regression test sends every optional metadata field as `null` and asserts the request validates, plus a guard that an unknown extra field and a non-string `pluginId` are still rejected (so the relaxation is surgical).

## User Impact

Plugin and bridge callers that serialize missing optional approval metadata as `null` (rather than omitting the key) now successfully register approval requests instead of receiving a spurious `INVALID_REQUEST`. Nullable optional approval metadata is now accepted identically to omitted metadata, matching the handler's existing behavior.

## Evidence

Reproduced on a clean checkout of `upstream/main` (`0f3fb9ea58`) before the fix, then re-ran the exact same command after:

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/gateway-protocol/src/plugin-approvals-validators.test.ts`

**Before** (schema rejects `null` — the two nullable-acceptance cases fail):

```
FAIL  ... > accepts nullable optional metadata the same as omitted metadata
AssertionError: expected false to be true
FAIL  ... > accepts a single nullable optional field alongside present metadata
AssertionError: expected false to be true
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
```

**After** (all optional metadata as `null` is accepted; the surgical guards still reject unknown fields and non-null invalid values):

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  4 passed (4)
```

The direct consumer suite is unaffected: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/plugin-approval.test.ts` → 60 passed (2 files). `oxlint` on the changed files is clean.

---

Note: draft #98404 addresses the same issue. It is currently draft, ~8 days stale, and `DIRTY`/conflicting against `main` (the schema has since gained the `approvalReviewerDeviceIds` field and the description max-length changed 256 → 512), and its `Real behavior proof` check fails. This PR is a fresh, non-draft change against current `main` with regression coverage and the PR-body evidence the gate requires. Happy to close this if a maintainer prefers to land #98404 instead.

target.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching and native Responses continuation
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived embedded sessions could lose prompt-cache continuity in three connected ways:

- ambient `room_event` turns changed cache-visible delivery instructions and owner-only tool schemas;
- queued work and preflight, manual, queued, or direct compaction rebuilt prompt/tool state from the current turn's effective delivery mode instead of the session-stable prompt mode;
- the built-in authenticated session stream was mistaken for a custom stream, so `openai-chatgpt-responses` runs bypassed OpenClaw's native cached WebSocket continuation path and replayed full context over managed SSE.

## Fix

- Separate effective source delivery from the session-stable prompt-facing mode. Room events still require `message_tool_only` delivery without rewriting the cached prompt contract.
- Construct executable Pi and Codex `message` tools with the real turn mode, preserving the internal source-reply sink and best-effort behavior; use the stable mode only for model-visible prompt/tool shape.
- Keep one safe room-event owner-only core-tool inventory across sender changes while preserving runtime authorization.
- Carry the prompt-facing mode through primary runs, queued followups, memory flushes, Codex app-server prompt/tool builders, and every compaction entry point.
- Keep Codex reusable thread instructions stable and add strict room-event delivery guidance only to the current turn.
- Mark OpenClaw's built-in session auth wrapper and allow only that known wrapper to select native `openai-chatgpt-responses` continuation. Unmarked custom/provider streams retain their existing routing.

The native route selection is API-based, so it covers GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 without model-version branches.

## Evidence

Redacted same-session traces from the reported Discord flow showed tool inventory flipping between 44 and 47 tools and cache reads collapsing to roughly 2k-10k or ceilinging around 37k-40k. With stable prompt/tool shape installed, warm turns reached roughly 49k-52k cached tokens on approximately 51k-55k context.

Behavioral coverage also proves:

- a targetless room-event `message(action=send)` still lands in the internal source-reply sink as `message_tool_only`;
- a two-turn GPT-5.6 Sol WebSocket run sends the second turn with `previous_response_id` and delta-only input instead of replaying full context;
- all supported compaction entry points rebuild from the stable prompt-facing mode.

## Validation

Validated at head `f0d85b0829d54ec9f3bda3406168f8bf2d8c0d6d` on upstream `main` `8dedb0ebcaef2bbe6dcd7b9ad137554b62ac1d21`:

- focused regression suite: 25 project test files, 1,211 tests passed;
- 219 focused Codex/source-delivery tests passed after the final review fixes;
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm tsgo:test:packages`, and the 120-plugin extension package boundary compile passed;
- changed TypeScript passed `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint`; generated prompt snapshots are current;
- all GitHub checks pass, including Real Behavior Proof;
- the exact head is installed locally with gateway RPC healthy and HTTP 200.

## Compatibility And Boundaries

- Effective room-event delivery remains strict; private final text does not become visible.
- Ambient `room_event` turns intentionally use the safe non-owner owner-only core-tool inventory for every sender so their prompt/tool contract stays cache-stable. Owner-only tools such as `cron`, `gateway`, `nodes`, and `computer` are therefore not prompt-visible on those ambient turns.
- Runtime authorization remains enforced; non-owner execution of owner-only tools is still blocked.
- Custom provider/session streams are not rerouted.
- Native `auto` transport may still fall back to SSE after a real WebSocket failure; this change makes native continuation reachable and tested, but does not claim every upstream request will be cached.

The remaining merge decision is whether maintainers accept the cache-stable safe inventory for ambient room events. ClawSweeper found no contributor-facing line-level blocker.

Disclaimer: This PR was filed and updated autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter. Private user, channel, host, credential, and full trace identifiers were removed from the evidence.

target.title: fix(google-meet): actually leave the Meet call in the browser on leave (#103386)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #103386.

`openclaw googlemeet leave <session-id>` on the Chrome transports printed `left <session-id>` and marked the session `ended`, but only ran the registered stop hook (the realtime audio bridge; in transcribe mode nothing at all). No code path touched the meeting, so the browser participant kept sitting in the call — a ghost participant receiving audio/captions after the operator was told it left. Twilio sessions already end the real call via their stop hook, so the transports were inconsistent.

### Change

- `extensions/google-meet/src/transports/chrome.ts`: new `leaveChromeMeet` / `leaveChromeMeetOnNode` (shared `leaveMeetWithBrowserRequest` core). It finds the session's Meet tab, clicks Meet's **Leave call** button via browser evaluate (reliable now that tabs are pinned to `?hl=en`), then closes the tab so departure is guaranteed even when the click misses. Failures degrade to session notes instead of throwing — `leave` still ends the session.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts`: `leave()` calls the browser leave for `chrome`/`chrome-node` sessions and records the outcome in session notes. Two guards:
  - the internal tab-reassignment path in `join()` passes `keepBrowserTab: true` so agent handoff keeps the in-call tab and avoids lobby re-admission;
  - a shared-tab guard skips closing while another active session still uses the same Meet tab.
- `docs/plugins/google-meet.md`: `leave` row now documents the Chrome-transport behavior.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` — 17 files, 208 tests passed (includes 3 new tests: browser leave click+close, no-matching-tab leave still ends the session with a note, and a vm test that the leave script clicks only an enabled Leave call button).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — clean.
- `pnpm format` / oxlint on touched files — clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: `googlemeet leave` leaves the browser participant in the Google Meet call on chrome/chrome-node transports while reporting `left`.
Real environment tested: No live Google Meet call was run; behavior is proven at the browser-proxy request boundary with the plugin's existing stubbed-gateway test harness (same harness the join/status paths use).
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` and `pnpm test extensions/google-meet/index.test.ts`.
Evidence after fix: New test "leaves the Meet call in the browser when a chrome session leaves" asserts the `/act` evaluate carries the leave-click script against the session tab and that `DELETE /tabs/local-meet-tab` is issued; session notes record "Clicked Meet's Leave call button and closed the Meet tab."
Observed result after fix: 208/208 tests pass; leave now issues real browser actions and the session ends with an explanatory note when no tab matches.
What was not tested: A live Meet meeting (real Chrome, real Google account) and the chrome-node transport against a physical node; both share `leaveMeetWithBrowserRequest`, which is covered by the harness.

target.title: fix(agents): surface provider server-side model fallbacks as lifecycle fallback_step events
target.body:
## Problem

Since #99906, Anthropic can re-serve a Claude Fable 5 request that its safety classifiers declined on Claude Opus 4.8 within a single API call (server-side fallback). The transport layer records the switch as a `provider_fallback` diagnostic on the assistant message and re-attributes `responseModel` — but nothing announces it. The TUI model indicator keeps showing the requested model, and the turn looks like a normal reply. Operators only discover the capability swap by inspecting webchat message details or the raw transcript.

This matters in practice: the `cyber`/`bio` classifiers are documented to false-positive on benign security and life-sciences work, so users doing exactly that work silently get Opus-served answers mid-conversation.

## Fix

Bridge the recorded diagnostic to the lifecycle `fallback_step` event shape the model-failover chain already emits (`phase: "fallback_step"`, `fallbackStepToModel: "provider/model"`). Existing consumers — the TUI model indicator (`applyFallbackStepModelUpdate`) and observability sinks — then present provider-served fallbacks exactly like chain fallbacks, with zero TUI changes.

- New `embedded-agent-subscribe.provider-fallback-notice.ts`: scans assistant-message diagnostics for `provider_fallback`, emits one lifecycle event per diagnostic. `fallbackStepSource: "provider_server_side"` distinguishes provider-served steps from chain steps without changing how current consumers parse the shared fields. Falls back to the message model when the boundary block omits `fromModel`; skips entries without a serving model.
- Wired into `handleMessageEnd` before visible-output suppression, so a served-by-fallback turn updates status surfaces even when reply text is suppressed.

## Relationship to in-flight work

#99472 (refusals trigger the OpenClaw fallback chain) covers the *client-side* chain path, which already has visible UX via these same events. This PR covers the *server-side* path from #99906, reusing the identical event shape so both mechanisms present uniformly. No conflict — different emission points.

## Testing

- New unit tests (6 cases: happy path, fromModel fallback, fromModel omission, no-diagnostic, missing toModel, missing provider) — pass in both shards
- `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.messages.test.ts` — 90/90 pass with the wire-in
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean, oxlint clean, prettier applied

target.title: fix(auth): use Set-based O(1) lookup for ownerAllowFrom authorization (#50289)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #50289 — deployments with large `commands.ownerAllowFrom` lists (9000+ entries) experience severe message processing latency (15-27s per message). Every incoming message triggers O(n) authorization checks via `Array.includes()` on the resolved owner list.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `Array.includes()` (O(n)) with `Set.has()` (O(1)) for owner list membership checks in command authorization:

1. **`OwnerAuthorizationState`** — added `ownerListSet` and `ownerCandidatesForCommandsSet` fields (internal type, not exported)
2. **`resolveCommandAuthorization`** — changed two `.includes()` lookups to `.has()` on the pre-built Sets
3. **`resolveCommandSenderAuthorization`** — builds a Set from `commandsAllowFromList` for O(1) sender candidate matching

The arrays are preserved in the state type — no public API change.

## User Impact

- Message processing latency drops from 15-27s to normal (<1s) for deployments with large ownerAllowFrom lists
- No behavior change — owner authorization logic is identical, only the data structure for lookups differs

## Evidence

- **5 test cases** in `command-auth.owner-allowfrom-perf.test.ts`:
  - Owner identification from 5000-entry list ✓
  - Non-owner rejection from 5000-entry list ✓
  - Channel-prefixed entry matching ✓
  - Cross-provider isolation (telegram entry doesn't grant discord) ✓
  - Performance proof: 100 resolutions × 10,000 entries in <1s ✓
- Existing `command-auth.owner-default.test.ts` tests continue to pass (same behavior contract)

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.


## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:


Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```

```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Summary

- Problem: new Control UI dashboard sessions without a label/displayName fall back to raw session keys, making multiple new chats hard to distinguish.

- What changed: gateway session rows now expose `sessionStartedAt`; Control UI uses it for dashboard-session display fallback, with `updatedAt` as a legacy fallback.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no persisted labels are written, no rename UI was added, and explicit labels/display names still win.

## Motivation

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
